feature: A calm redline of a UI screenshot
summary: Asking Ask to "annotate the ux with measurements around the major ui elements" now lays the redline a designer hands a developer: one size of each kind of control, then the spacing that defines the layout, with no readout on another readout, on words or on a control. Code chooses the marks off the picture; the model only confirms them.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: ask-annotates-a-screenshot-walk (the settings screenshot), ask-redlines-a-dialog-walk, ask-redlines-a-feed-walk.

try.do: Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png. This was your picture before: twelve measurements, the switch measured four times, readouts stacked.
Press Ask, type "annotate the ux with measurements around the major ui elements" and send.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read the Measurements list: Switch, Field and Button once each, then Padding, Row height, Section gap, Gap and Label inset.
Look for two readouts touching, or a readout on a label, a switch or a field.
Press Command Z once: the whole redline goes in one step.
Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/misalign/dialog-clean.png and ask the same: one button size for the row of three, padding, gap and label inset.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/misalign/feed-clean.png and ask the same: the avatar once, padding, the gap between cards, avatar to name.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Is one size per kind of control (on whichever has the most room) what you want, or should the size always sit on the first one?
Is this the spacing you would mark: padding, row height, the gap between sections and between buttons, a button's label inset?
Does any readout still read as belonging to the wrong thing?
Is leaving out the margin to the screenshot's own edge right? It is where the picture was cropped, not part of the design.
rough: Readouts still say px on a 2x screenshot (42 for the 84 pixel switch is points, labelled px as the Measure tool always has). The eval's judge reads "124 px" on a 248 pixel button as wrong. Filed as a-redline-of-a-2x-screenshot-reads-in-points-wit.

The settings case scores 47 to 59 for Ask (32.5 before; the same picture moved 12 points between two judgings) and the judge gives clean 4, not the 8 the task asked for. Its remaining complaints are the caliper look: no end ticks, Size brackets that do not plainly show what they span. Same follow-up: a-redline-of-a-2x-screenshot-reads-in-points-wit. The skill engine lays the identical redline (judge 4.2; its old 62.8 was on the previous rubric).

Eval totals for Ask: climb 79.1 (was 78.2), held-out 19.5 (was 20.1, inside the noise). But the held-out redline group fell from 35.4 to 19.6, twice in a row, and the rules keep a runner from reading those cases. Filed as ask-s-redlines-do-at-least-as-well-on-unseen-req; the final held-out run's pictures are at .ask-eval/held-out-runs/20261021-055152-ask-held-out/contact-sheet.png for you to look at.

Measurements placed by hand still use the Measure tool's own placer, whose leash and on-the-line behaviour you chose; the redline placer shares its candidates and the one label placer but adds hard rules. Bringing those rules to hand placement is in a-redline-of-a-2x-screenshot-reads-in-points-wit.
A mark with no clean spot for its readout is left out rather than stacked, down to three marks; below that the rest land as the Measure tool would place them.
No mock covers this surface: the redline uses the Measure tool's existing look.
